title: OpenAI will start watermarking ChatGPT’s text in the EU
key_facts: OpenAI will start adding an invisible watermark to text generated by ChatGPT and Codex in the EU to comply with the EU AI Act, the company said Monday in a blog post.
The AI Act's transparency rules, which took effect on 2 August, require AI companies to mark AI-generated content in a way other systems can identify.

The watermark rolls out over the coming weeks to eligible ChatGPT and Codex users on all plans, in the EU only; developers using OpenAI's API anywhere in the world can switch it on for select models from Monday, but it is off by default, and OpenAI is not making text watermarking a global default at launch.

It works by subtly shaping the model's word choices, leaving a pattern readers cannot see but a detector can pick up, and it travels with the text when copied and pasted; OpenAI says it does not identify the user and caused no meaningful change in its models' performance.
OpenAI also published a technical report on the method, called textGrain, co-written with researchers from the University of Pennsylvania and Yale.

OpenAI's tests suggest editing can remove the mark: replacing 10% of words with synonyms cut detection from about 92% to 66%; short passages, math answers and translated text are also harder to detect.

Because of these limits, initial detector access goes only to approved researchers and expert organizations; OpenAI cautions that a missing watermark does not prove human authorship, since the text could be too short, too heavily edited or from another company's AI.

Context from TechCrunch: Anthropic said two months ago it would watermark text generated by Claude worldwide, which drew backlash from some users; OpenAI had built a text watermark earlier but held off, partly over fears users would switch to rivals, according to a 2024 Wall Street Journal report.
